subject: Aster Labs — aligning per-call accounting with session history (pilot scope)
messages:
From: Jenna Park <jenna.park@asterlabs.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 08 Jan 2027 12:04:00 -05:00
Subject: Pilot billing question: short chats vs long-history retrievals

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the time earlier. A quick follow-up from procurement as we finalize the SOW: we need a concise explanation of how Redwood will bill the different flows in our pilot. Specifically: 

- Short customer-facing support chats that are typically 40–120 tokens per turn (we expect many of these).
- Background/history lookups where the assistant pulls a 6–10k token conversation context to answer (not every request — maybe 2–3% of calls).

Two procurement questions: 1) if a single UI action triggers a streaming response + a small follow-up (two API calls), are those treated as separate billable requests or grouped? 2) how do rounding/minimums apply to very small calls — do you round to a fixed quantum, or is there a per-call minimum dollar amount?

Can you also share a sample invoice row for: (a) 100k small-chat calls averaging 80 tokens each and (b) 2k long-history requests averaging 6,500 tokens. We just need a storable example for our finance team.

I attached the latest SOW for context.

Best,
Jenna
Procurement, Aster Labs

[Attachment: Aster_Pilot_SOW_v1.docx (DOCX)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@asterlabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 09 Jan 2027 18:32:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot billing question: short chats vs long-history retrievals

Jenna — thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise explanation plus a linked sample CSV (attached) that maps to the two scenarios. I kept the math conservative so finance can see worst-case. Happy to walk through live.

TL;DR summary
- Billable units are computed per API request based on tokenized input + tokenized output (we call this the request token total).
- For pilot customers we apply a small-call floor and a billing quantum to limit microbilling noise: floor = 24 tokens per request; quantum = 16 tokens.
- Rounding: once request tokens are totaled, we round up to the nearest quantum (16-token increments). The floor (24 tokens) is enforced before quantum rounding.
- Multi-call grouping: separate HTTP calls are billed separately unless routed by the same request id in the SDK (explicit session bundling). Our streaming segments are still part of the single request if they were sent with the same call id; post-response follow-ups are separate requests unless batched client-side.

Worked examples (numbers in tokens) — included as CSV attachment (pilot_invoice_sample.csv).
1) Small-chat: 100,000 calls · average request tokens = 80
   - Per-call billable tokens: max(80, 24) = 80 -> round up to nearest 16 => 80 already multiple of 16 => 80 tokens billed per call
   - Total billed tokens = 100,000 * 80 = 8,000,000 tokens

2) Long-history: 2,000 calls · average request tokens = 6,500
   - Per-call billable tokens: max(6500, 24) = 6500 -> round up to nearest 16 => 6,504 tokens billed per call
   - Total billed tokens = 2,000 * 6,504 = 13,008,000 tokens

3) Combined invoice row example (CSV attaches): 
   - Line A: small-chat, 8,000,000 tokens, unit price $0.0000125/token => $100.00
   - Line B: long-history, 13,008,000 tokens, unit price $0.0000125/token => $162.60
   - Note: prices in the sample are illustrative; the SOW’s negotiated unit price will populate the invoice generator.

Cache/kv reuse note
- If a long-history request benefits from KV/prefix reuse (i.e., identical prompt prefixes retrieved from same conversation cache), the runtime will deduct cached tokens from the billable input count per our KV-credit policy. The sample intentionally assumes no cache credits.

Streaming specifics
- Streaming chunks emitted during the same API call count towards the request’s output tokens and are not billed as separate calls. If you terminate streaming and then immediately send another request, that second call is billed independently unless your client attaches the session tag for server-side bundling.

Edge cases and credits
- Microburst protection: for calls under the floor that were generated by automated health pings or heartbeats, we offer a monthly microburst credit reconciliation (applied as a single invoice adjustment) if you share logs for us to validate.

Next steps
- I attached pilot_invoice_sample.csv with the exact rows you requested. If acceptable, we can add a one-line clause to the SOW that documents the floor + quantum used for the pilot (recommended).

Thanks — I’ll also loop in Sales for a limited pilot discount proposal if Aster wants a price cushion during onboarding.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Platform Partnerships, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pilot_invoice_sample.csv (CSV)]

From: Jenna Park <jenna.park@asterlabs.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Pilot billing question: short chats vs long-history retrievals

Thanks Irene — this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifications from procurement and finance: 

- When you say "round up to nearest 16 tokens" for long-history requests, do you round per request or per invoice line? (We prefer per-request rounding for predictability.)
- For streaming: if the assistant emits an initial 2k-token answer and then a client asks a 30-token follow-up in the same UI, but that follow-up is sent as a new API call, we want to understand if you can detect "same user interaction" and group for billing. Is session bundling something we can enable in the pilot SDK config?

Also, procurement asked if Redwood is open to a pilot discount: 10% off list if we exceed 1.5M billed tokens in the first 30 days. We’re not asking for a long-term commit, just a limited onboarding concession. Timeline: we need a one-page pricing appendix in the SOW by Jan 15.

Appreciate it — Jenna
